newsitem.title: USA: California's unemployment rate drops to 6.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: California's unemployment rate drops to 6.5 pct.

text.p: California's unemployment rate dropped to 6.5 percent in March from a revised 6.6 percent in February, the state said on Friday.
The unemployment rate last year in March was 7.5 percent, the Employment Development Department reported.
If the pace of job growth during the past six months continues through 1997, the state will add well over 400,000 jobs during the year, the department said.
California businesses have now added more than one million new jobs since the end of the job recession in April 1993, with a net gain of 41,300 jobs since the February survey.
"California's economy is in the midst of a strong expansion," Gov. Pete Wilson said in a statement lauding the state's latest employment figures.
The number of people employed in California was 14,791,000 in March, an increase of 45,000 over the month and up 422,000 compared with March 1996, the Employment Development Department said.

The number of unemployed continues to decline, down 6,000 over the month and down 139,000 over the year. The number of unemployed in March was 1,033,000, the lowest number since November 1990, the department said.

Seven industry sectors added jobs in March, while two industries -- mining and finance, insurance and real estate -- reported job declines amounting to a loss of 600 jobs, the department said. Most of the job growth was in the service sector, up 22,100 jobs.
